text:
sam: prod alerts — a handful of inference replicas hit OOMs during longctx workloads after today's rollout. Spike at ~03:12 UTC, QPS unchanged, latency mostly fine but OOMs saw immediate error rates.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout 2026-03-17T02:58Z applied by li (commit abc1234). canary -> 50% -> 100%; autoscale 8->12 nodes.

li: grabbing logs now. are failures only on >4k token requests or elsewhere?

sasha: only longctx so far. grabbed one core dump and heapmap, attaching snippet:
```
heap_total: 48GB
kv_reserved: 38GB
kv_active: 36.4GB
kv_free_frag: 4.8GB
kv_slab_free_ratio: 7%
hot_slab_count: 1120 -> high churn
sequence_len_bucket: >4096 shows 3x allocation spikes
```

elena: can we revert the rollout while we triage? this is causing user errors.

li: starting a bisect. disabling further canary promotion. quick local bisect points at commit def4567 — message: "autobatch: shrink boundary for kernel-A when p50 < latency_target".

sasha: looking at perf traces: after merge kernel-selection switches a lot of longctx requests to kernel-A (lower latency for short sequences). kernel-A's allocator layout uses denser pagelets but smaller reservation windows. combined with the new autobatch heuristic we now end up with many small inflight batches for long requests -> high slab fragmentation and reserve exhaustion.

sam: so the root isn't eviction policy itself, it's an interaction: kernel selection + autobatch + allocator.

li: yes. eviction thresholds didn't change. what changed is average batch size distribution for long sequences (shift left), which increases the number of hot allocations living concurrently and prevents coalescing.

oncall: rolled back def4567 at 03:40 UTC and paused rollout. observed immediate drop in OOMs on the affected fleet. putting rollout on hold.

infra-bot: rollback complete by elena (revert-gh-890) at 03:41Z.

sasha: repro in staging by forcing kernel-A + longctx load reproduces OOM quickly. local quickfix: bump soft-reserve for kernel-A by 25% and increase allocator coalesce window to 128ms. quickfix PR: gh/rl-1234. snippet:
```yaml
# allocator tweaks
kernel_A:
  soft_reserve_multiplier: 1.25
  coalesce_window_ms: 128
autobatch:
  min_boundary_for_longseq: 32  # temporary guard
```

li: longer term we should change autobatch heuristic. current rule shrinks boundary purely on p50 latency; that punishes longtail batches. proposal: make boundary adapt using sequence-length distribution (p90 seqlen) + latency.

elena: filing rollout blocker ticket and adding a longctx synthetic job to perf CI (so merges that affect long-seq behavior fail fast). also add fragmentation alert on heaplet free ratio <10%.

sam: :+1: include reproducible curl for staging so oncall/sre can run the test. sasha, can you paste the curl?

sasha: sure — staging repro:
```bash
curl -X POST https://staging-infer.redwood.dev/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" \
  -H "X-Force-Kernel: kernel-A" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":5000,"client_seq_len":6000}'
```

li: opened TICKET-5121 (rollout-blocker) with bisect notes, repro, heapmap, and temporary mitigations. assigned to eng-runtime + eng-platform.

elena: postmortem action items: (1) add kernel-choice vs batch-size telemetry, (2) add longctx perf job to CI with mem/frag assertions, (3) document soft-pin semantics and allocator coalesce knobs, (4) implement autobatch guard for longseq.

sam: closing loop for now — revert live, monitoring for 24h. follow-ups tracked in TICKET-5121. thanks for the quick triage.
